There is a reason why my tutor straight up told us to not even touch the NP essay question in Finals after he saw the paper. He knew that with the added time pressure, attempting such questions is basically giving up the free 0.5 marks for leaving questions blank. People who attempted it probably have brain loss or actually accurately spotted the question and have the tech to answer it correctly. This module really took up a lot of time and effort, especially mentally. The semester was meant to be a somewhat relaxing one essentially 1.5 CS modules so I could focus on learning Japanese, but this module really wanted me to stay monolingual (We do not talk about Chinese). I must say I really lucked out with the grading in the end though. Throughout the semester, I genuinely was happy getting my first C or another B-, but having a friend who took the module the semester before and is embracing his masochistic tendencies by taking CS3231 and CS4234 (both follow-ups to CS3230) at the same time benefitted a lot (ignore LPS reduction question). I was just barely able to max out my CA 40%, and did perform above average for Midterm (Bless None of the above options and Naive solutions). Finals MCQ did not go as well, but hail mary attempts at answering some questions parts and somehow logically deducing what a clique (actual miracle) helped edge my grade over to a B+ which I most definitely am happy about. As much as I hate the content, and potentially the cohort taking this module (maybe just the CS cohort in general), I did enjoy the teaching staff, specifically my TA Alvin who honestly is just a chill guy. Prof YiJun was great this semester too, given it is his first time and while there's many controversies surrounding him now, Prof Halim still deserves his props for making the module that slight bit more bearable.
closingRemarks: If you can fly out, map it overseas. If you can't, just take it and pray.

name: CS4226: Internet Archictecture
intro: Supposedly low workload Level-4000 CS module that is also part of the easiet Focus Area to complete.
review: The module started with slightly dry content: small refresher on CS2105 concepts while introducing a few new ones such as Little Law and Min Max Fair Allocation. The first half generally did not have a lot of content to cover. A lot of it was just the understanding of different concepts and a revisit of statistics and probability concepts, namely the Poisson process. There were wuite a lot of new formula and definitions but the exams where open book with online resources allowed as well, so it was not too much of an issue. The midterm was hence relatively easy to prepare for since it was all MCQ and there just didn't seem like there was enough content to test at all. This is where the written assignment was released. but it honestly sort of a recitation/revision worksheet instead and the 10% came from filling out a survey on the difficulty of the questions from the WA. Second half of the module covered more interesting concepts on SDN, ASes and BGP but sadly it was not deliverd as well as the content in the first half. The Prof did say he was not as comfortable with the more fluffy content as comapred to the math aspect so that should be considered. Still, it was a shame because when revising the second half content, I can definitely see msyself taking an interest to some of the topics covered. As for the programming assignments, content wise, it ranges in difficulty. The tasks were either more menial in nature or require reading a lot of documentation to figure things out, at least from personal experience. It also did not help that networks is more niche and such content is not as readily available online as something like a simple BFS for example. Nonetheless, investing enough time will eventually net you the solution. This is basically the only workload anyway, so no harm putting in the effort here. My one gripe with the PAs would be the test scripts though. PA2 had no proper test scripts and it wasn't clear what exactly we should be looking out for and the other 2 PAs had test scripts that took a really long time to run. But I guess that is just the nature of the content and I can't really blame the teaching staff for it. One thing I can blame the teaching staff for however would be the Piazza forum. It started off rather quiet but began teeming with queries and posts when the PAs were released. The Prof and the TAs were somewhat active in the beginning butas the weeks went by, they started becoming less responsive and were not consistent in replying questions. It also seemed weird that they would prioritize answering certain questions quickly but completely ghosting another person's request for advice. Just didn't sit right with me. To wrap up, Finals was somewhat similar to the Midterm, maybe a tad bit trickier but all in all still manageable. Nothing much else to say about the module.
closingRemarks: Honestly did not feel like a Level-4000 module but I will take it. Do take note if you are team Apple, have fun configuring your VMs lol. You won't get a lot of help.
